::: {.callout-important}
## Use the official protocol at the bench
This page is a planning and checklist summary. Run the library prep from Oxford Nanopore's own protocol for your kit version (log in to the [Nanopore Community](https://community.nanoporetech.com/)). Nanopore kits change often, and newer direct RNA kits and flow cells may have replaced SQK-RNA002 / R9.4.1, so check what is current before ordering.
:::

## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Input** | **500 ng total RNA** or **50 ng poly(A) RNA** in 9 µL nuclease-free water |
| **Output** | Native-RNA reads (no RT or PCR bias; base modifications retained) |
| **Kits** | Direct RNA Sequencing Kit SQK-RNA002; Flow Cell Priming Kit EXP-FLP002; R9.4.1 flow cell FLO-MIN106; Flow Cell Wash Kit EXP-WSH004 |
| **Device** | MinION Mk1B/Mk1C with MinKNOW |
| **Time** | ~2 h library prep + ~15 min priming/loading, then sequencing |

## Why direct RNA

Use it to study native RNA (e.g. base modifications), to avoid reverse transcription and PCR bias, or for transcripts that are hard to reverse-transcribe. The RT step in the prep only makes a cDNA strand to stabilize the RNA; the **RNA strand** is what passes through the pore.

## Third-party materials to have ready

- SuperScript III reverse transcriptase + 5× first-strand buffer + 0.1 M DTT
- 10 mM dNTPs
- NEBNext Quick Ligation Reaction Buffer; T4 DNA ligase (2 M U mL⁻¹)
- Agencourt RNAClean XP beads; freshly made 70% ethanol (nuclease-free water)
- Qubit RNA HS and dsDNA HS assays
- 1.5 mL DNA LoBind tubes, 0.2 mL PCR tubes, nuclease-free water
- Hula mixer, magnetic rack, thermal cycler, Qubit; Bioanalyzer/TapeStation optional

## Before you start

- **Check RNA quality**: length, quantity and purity are critical (Qubit + TapeStation/Bioanalyzer).
- **Check the flow cell**: run a flow cell check in MinKNOW and confirm enough active pores.
- **Install/update MinKNOW** on the device or computer.

## Workflow at a glance

| Stage | What happens | Key amounts |
|---|---|---|
| 1. RT adapter ligation | RNA + RT adapter (RTA) + RNA CS control, ligated 10 min at RT | 9 µL RNA in a 15 µL reaction |
| 2. Reverse transcription | Make the cDNA strand with SuperScript III: 50 °C 50 min → 70 °C 10 min → 4 °C | 40 µL reaction |
| 3. Bead cleanup | RNAClean XP beads, two 70% ethanol washes, elute | 72 µL beads; elute in 20 µL water |
| 4. RNA adapter ligation | Ligate the motor-protein adapter (RMX), 10 min at RT | 40 µL reaction |
| 5. Bead cleanup | RNAClean XP beads, **2× Wash Buffer (WSB)** washes (no ethanol), elute | 16 µL beads; elute in 21 µL Elution Buffer, 10 min |
| 6. QC | Qubit dsDNA HS on 1 µL | Aim for **~20 ng** recovered |
| 7. Prime flow cell | Flush Tether into Flush Buffer; remove air bubble from the priming port; prime | 800 µL, wait 5 min, then 200 µL |
| 8. Load | Library in RNA Running Buffer, added dropwise to the SpotON port | 37.5 µL RRB + 37.5 µL library (20 µL library + 17.5 µL water) = 75 µL |
| 9. Sequence | Start the run in MinKNOW (basecalling in real time) | |

## Critical tips

- **Wash with WSB, not ethanol**, after the RMX ligation (stage 5). Ethanol damages the motor protein on the adapter.
- **Flick the beads** during WSB washes rather than just adding and removing buffer; agitation removes free adapter much better.
- **No air bubbles** in the priming port or sensor array: draw back 20–30 µL before priming and pipette slowly.
- Mix RNA by **flicking**, not vortexing, to avoid shearing.
- Load the library **dropwise**, letting each drop enter the SpotON port before adding the next.
